source_excerpt: [F6] [[thm-fundamental-theorem-for-autonomous-smooth-odes]]: a smooth autonomous vector field has a local flow smooth in the initial state on a common time neighborhood.
proposed_replacement: [F6] [[lem-c1-euclidean-maximal-flow-with-c2-upgrade]]: a $C^1$ autonomous vector field has a jointly $C^1$ local flow, unique trajectories, and a continuous first state derivative satisfying its variational equation. For the $C^1$ nonautonomous radial equation on $r>0$, adjoining $\theta'=1$ and $\beta'=0$ gives the same joint $C^1$ dependence on radius and parameter; no fifth derivative of a flow is used.

On $r>0$ the radial field is jointly $C^1$ in $(\theta,r,\beta)$ by the finite-regularity coordinate construction in [F4]. Applying [F6] to $(\theta,r,\beta)'=(1,\rho(\theta,r,\beta),0)$ gives the required common local solution and first variations, with finite composition over $[0,2\pi]$. For small $r_0>0$ and $|\beta|$, while $r\in[r_0/2,2r_0]$ the bound $|\rho/r|\le C(|\beta|+4r_0^2)$ makes the change in $\log r$ over $[0,2\pi]$ smaller than $\log2$. source_excerpt: 5.1 The Poincare derivative is a smooth local map by [F4]'s hypotheses, has no unit-circle multiplier, and all its eigenvalues are strictly inside. Apply [F5] to conclude orbital asymptotic stability.
proposed_replacement: 5.1 The certificate field is $C^2$ and its affine phase section is smooth; [F4]'s hypotheses therefore give a $C^1$ Poincare return map. Its derivative has no unit-circle multiplier, and all its eigenvalues are strictly inside by step 4.1. Apply the $C^1$ theorem [F5] to conclude orbital asymptotic stability.
